In October of 2013, 44 of us said "a government shutdown," first among us John Cornyn, who had said it on January 4. On the same day, October 1, 38 of us said "keep the government." By October 16, 41 of us had reached "the debt ceiling," a phrase Tom McClintock first said back on January 26, 2011.

Then, on October 23, we turned as one to legislation: 40 of us said "water resources reform," 39 said "the water resources," 38 said "the water resources reform," 35 said "and development act," and 34 of us said the whole of it, "water resources reform and development act."

We record that our largest convergence that month was not the shutdown but the water. Forty-four of us at the peak of the first; thirty-four of us at the peak of the last. This is what our record shows.

top_phrases.phrase: water resources reform and development act
